thread:
Maria Chen: Heads-up — I noticed the cache hit-rate split by deployment looks odd for redwood-xxl-v1. Hosted avg hit-rate ~62% but Dedicated pools are at ~40% for the same route set. Screenshot: https://grafana.internal/d/abc123/cache-breakdown :eyes:
Raj Patel: Hmm, do we have model-version pinning differences? Hosted might be on v1.2.1 and Dedicated on v1.1.8 which had different KV key hashing.
Maria Chen: Good call. I checked model tags — both report v1.2.1. Kernel selection should be identical.
TJ: Could be request fanout / route sharding. Dedicated pools serve more enterprise routes with long context -> longer prefix variance -> lower prefix reuse.
Olivia K: I can pull route-level slices. Which metrics should I look at? cache_hit_rate, cache_lookups, tokens_saved, and distinct_prefixes. Anything else?
Samir: Add cache_key_entropy and avg_prefix_length. If entropy goes up, hit-rate will drop even with same traffic.
Raj Patel: Also look at batching heuristics: Dedicated uses tail-batching config 2.0-optimized which may produce different sequence length distributions and cause fewer identical cache accesses in the same batch window.
Kai: Another dimension — KV cache churn per-tenant. If Dedicated has smaller KV stores per GPU, eviction could be higher. Check kv_evictions_by_customer.
Maria Chen: Olivia — can you run a 7-day comparison of these panels broken out by deployment_type, route, and customer_tier? Prefer CSV export so I can do a quick pivot.
Olivia K: On it. Quick PromQL I'm running now (adapt if needed):
```
sum by(deployment_type, route) (cache_hits_total{model="redwood-xxl-v1"})
/ sum by(deployment_type, route) (cache_lookups_total{model="redwood-xxl-v1"})
```
Will also compute tokens saved per 1k: (tokens_saved_total / requests_total) * 1000.
dev-bot: Scheduled export job: cache-slice-export-2165432100 started (CSV -> /data/exports/cache_slices_2165432100.csv).
Raj Patel: While that's running, can we sanity-check the cache key normalization? We recently pushed a change that normalizes whitespace and strip-user-ids, maybe Dedicated routing skews inputs before normalizer.
Samir: I grep'd the logs — normalization noop looks identical on both. But I found a config diff: dedicated/kvcfg.yaml sets max_prefix_entries: 40, hosted sets 80. That'll affect eviction.
Maria Chen: That's significant. Any rationale?
TJ: Ops wanted smaller per-GPU footprint for Dedicated to increase tenant isolation. Might be a historical config. We should evaluate effective tokens_saved per GB to see tradeoffs.
Olivia K: Export done. Quick highlights: Dedicated has 38% hit-rate on routes /summarize and /qa for a set of enterprise customers, hosted has 68%. tokens_saved_per_1k: Dedicated ~420, Hosted ~980 on same routes. Distinct_prefixes per 1k reqs: Dedicated 870 vs Hosted 320.
Kai: Distinct prefixes >> suggests keying or input preprocessing differs. Could also be that Dedicated users include long multi-turn contexts with unique prefixes.
Raj Patel: Actionable checks: 1) confirm normalizer versions across control plane and Dedicated agents, 2) compare kvcfg max_prefix_entries and eviction policy, 3) run a synthetic replay of top 1000 prefixes against both deployments to measure hit-rate delta.
Maria Chen: I'll own #3. Olivia take #1 and #2?
Olivia K: I can do #1 quickly (versions) and #2 after lunch (talk to infra).
Samir: For the synthetic replay, use this script (pseudo):
```
# load top_prefixes.csv
for p in prefixes:
  send_request(route="/qa", model="redwood-xxl-v1", prompt=p)
  record(cache_hit)
```
We should run against a dedicated staging pool and hosted staging endpoint.
TJ: Also, dashboard idea — add a panel showing cache_hit_rate delta (hosted - dedicated) by route with a 7d rolling average, and a heatmap of tokens_saved_per_customer. That'll help spot tenants losing the most.
Kai: I can add the delta panel. Suggest color thresholds: >20% red, 10-20% orange.
Maria Chen: Temporary mitigation: can we bump max_prefix_entries on Dedicated pools for top-affected tenants? If it's a config toggle we can do a targeted change.
Raj Patel: We need a quick perf test because increasing entries increases memory pressure and may affect kernel selection for kv storage. Let's not blanket it.
Olivia K: Logged action: INFRA-1129 to review kvcfg and propose per-tenant overrides.
dev-bot: INFRA-1129 created by Olivia K.
Maria Chen: Next steps recap: Olivia verify normalizer/version and file INFRA-1129. Maria run synthetic replay and share results by EOD tomorrow. Kai adds delta panel. Raj and Samir to run memory / eviction modelling for changing max_prefix_entries. TJ to assess batching heuristic impact on cache coalescing.
Samir: One more ask — add a lightweight histogram of time-to-first-cache-hit-per-request. It can surface warmup regressions where cache population is delayed.
Raj Patel: Good idea. Name it ttfch (time-to-first-cache-hit_ms).
Maria Chen: Thanks team. If any owner needs help, ping me. :thumbsup:
Olivia K: Uploading csv to #eng-data now: /data/exports/cache_slices_2165432100.csv
Maria Chen: Received. I'll start the replay script in staging.
Kai: I'll post the panel PR once ready.
Maria Chen: Closing loop later today with a short note on findings.
Maria Chen: (after replay) Quick update — synthetic replay shows a 52% hit-rate on Hosted staging vs 34% on Dedicated staging with identical request stream. Looks like config + eviction is main driver.
Raj Patel: Thanks. Let's keep Dedicated pool memory config as the primary suspect.
Maria Chen: Filing follow-up postmortem if we change configs.
